title: Drawing primitives: planar VGA and the software renderer
summary: The drawing core is in better shape than its comments. Its inner loops are written for the 8088's real costs: the fetch floor, the xchg latch idiom, a one-store read-modify-write, mask tables, and rep movsw with an adc tail. Clipping and display translation are handled once at the public entry and re-enter a single raw body, and unusual cases refuse with CF=1 and a fallback rather than approximating. The real defects sit at the edges. gfx_blit4 never checks the sign of its width, and a negative width passes both decoders' on-screen check. On VGA the planar decoder's group count wraps to ~65,536, sweeping the whole 64KB from the 336-byte vga_pbuf into the heap above .vgabuf; on 1bpp it writes ~8KB of framebuffer a row. The fix is zero bytes, and gfx_blitp already has it. The planar decoder's deliberate over-read is safe in real mode but plausibly a #GP on kern_mega's tight claim selectors. There are three systemic weaknesses: (1) each whole-shape primitive orders hide, display enter and depth dispatch by hand, and the comments record five field bugs from getting that order wrong; (2) a shelf of built-and-off KHP knob bodies doubles the reading surface without shipping their measured gains to the calibration machine; (3) the history-heavy comments now describe at least two dozen things that no longer exist. Cheap wins: delete one of the two CLIPQF checks in every gfx_blit1 band (-3 bytes on each kernel; a far call saved on kern_big), add a planar arm to gfx_points (5-10x per point on VGA, predicted), and pin the path-dependent [gfx_color] side effect of gfx_blit4.

strengths.title: One store per masked byte: dest ^= (pat ^ dest) & mask
strengths.why: Three bus accesses instead of four, and bits outside the mask are never written back stale even if an ISR touches the byte. It killed a real one-frame flash (tests/deskflash.py). Copy it to every remaining 1bpp RMW.

strengths.title: Clip and display hooks sit above the renderer dispatch and re-enter one raw body
strengths.why: One hook serves VGA, both 1bpp adapters and the packed driver. The virtual-before-translate ordering argument is written where it binds (544-550).

strengths.title: The right VGA idioms
strengths.evidence: vga12.inc:259-293 (8,mask word pair), 3403-3436 xchg latch+masked write, 3483-3495 XOR interior as rep movsb over itself, 5276-5350 write-mode-1 scroll
strengths.why: These are the tricks the Windows 3.x VGA driver used, in a fraction of the code, and they are priced against the 8088.

strengths.title: Derived tables built from one source of truth and unioned
strengths.evidence: softgfx.inc:879-922 sw_pairbuild; vga12.inc:2489-2526 vga_p4build; 7144-7165 union with built-flag word
strengths.why: The colour reduction lives only in gfx_inktab. 512 bytes of .lowbss serve both decoders, and each builder clears the other's flag in one store.

strengths.title: Refusal as contract, with probes
strengths.evidence: vga12.inc:2927-2940 (gfx_blitp DI bit 15), 3541-3545 gfx_spans, gfx_blit1 CF=1
strengths.why: Every caller has a correct slower path one branch away. This is §47 applied to primitives.

strengths.title: Per-row run-density pricing in gfx_blit4
strengths.why: The first run's length is the probe and the run count is the budget, both free from the scanner. Flat rows keep the span writer and dithered rows go to the transpose. Measured (Set 107).

strengths.title: Layout invariants are assembler errors
strengths.why: Every word load of a byte pair is guarded by %error at the declaration, so a re-layout fails the build instead of silently corrupting.

strengths.title: gfx_unlock ends the drawing transaction and resets all leakable state
strengths.why: Region, pen, mono1, disabled pen, display context, progress widget and busy shape all die with the hold, so a forgetful caller inherits the safe value. This is EndPaint's idea without an explicit release.

strengths.title: The .vga rung slide
strengths.why: It gets GEOS's 'only this adapter's driver is resident' while keeping near calls, which suits an 8088 better than GEOS's far strategy call.

findings.title: gfx_blit4 trusts the sign of its width; a negative width overruns vga_pbuf (VGA) or sprays the framebuffer (1bpp)
findings.detail: gfx_blit4 refuses only zero: `or cx,cx / jz vga_b4out`, and the same for DX. Both decoders then prove the block is on screen with an unsigned add that wraps (1bpp `add ax,cx / cmp ax,[vid_cw] / ja .slow`; planar `mov dx,ax / add dx,cx / cmp dx,[vid_cw] / ja .pdone`), and `cmp cx,16 / jb` passes any CX >= 16. Example: x=20, w=-10 (a package's x2-x1+1 on an empty rect) gives x+w = 10, which counts as on screen. On VGA the first row that opens on detail goes .eplanar into vga_blit_prow with CX ~ 0xFFF6. Its byte span comes from the wrapped last pixel x+w-1, which lies LEFT of x, so [vga_pr_n] = col(last) - col(x) + 1 is <= 0 (0 in the example). `dec bp / jnz .g` then runs ~65,536 groups, storing at [di], [di+84], [di+168] and [di+252] across the whole 64KB of VGABUF_SEG from vga_pbuf: the bottom of the heap above the kernel, corrupted by one bad package argument (a #GP on kern_mega's selector). On 1bpp (kern_big and kern_small), sw_blit_row writes ~8KB of framebuffer per row (32,763 pairs; on a dual-card Hercules, into the CGA's aperture). A negative DX is a ~65,535-row loop. gfx_blitp already fixed exactly this, citing PaccMan.
evidence: vga12.inc:1886-1889 jz only, no sign test
vga12.inc:2050-2054 planar x proof wraps; cx>=16 passes negatives
vga12.inc:2551-2570 n derived from the wrapped last x: <= 0 when w < 0, so BP wraps to ~65536 groups
vga12.inc:2608-2661 .g writes BP groups into vga_pbuf
vga12.inc:2856-2859 gfx_blitp's jle fix and PaccMan note
kernel.asm:2797-2798 OSAPI_SLOT gfx_blit4: no validation in the cell
findings.recommendation: Change `jz vga_b4out` to `jle vga_b4out` at both sites (same encoding: short backward jump). Optionally do the same for gfx_blit1_x's `jcxz .refuse` (softgfx-free, .cold +2 bytes), where the consequence is only framebuffer garbage.
findings.prior_art: Windows GDI normalises/rejects inverted rectangles at the DC layer before any driver sees them.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed by re-reading vga12.inc:1886-1889 (jz only), 2009-2013 and 2046-2054 (unsigned wrap), 2237-2249 (.eplanar) and 2551-2661 (vga_blit_prow). One detail corrected: on VGA the group count is not ~8190. With a negative w the last pixel x+w-1 lies LEFT of x, so n = col(last) - col(x) + 1 is 1 (same byte) or <= 0. Example x=20, w=-10: last=9, n=0, so `dec bp / jnz .g` runs 65,536 times. The stores at [di], [di+84], [di+168] and [di+252] then sweep the whole 64KB of VGABUF_SEG from vga_pbuf, which is the bottom of the heap above the kernel. ~8190 bytes is right for the 1bpp case (sw_blit_row: 32,763 pairs). kern_small (1bpp only, no GFX_PLANE) has the sw_blit_row half. On kern_mega the VGABUF selector's limit turns it into a #GP. `jle` is the same 2-byte short encoding as `jz`. Not listed in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.

findings.title: The planar decoder's deliberate over-read can #GP on kern_mega
findings.detail: vga_blit_prow starts the decode p>>1 bytes early and reads whole 4-byte groups, so it touches up to 3 bytes before a row's first source byte and up to 3 after its last. The code and SPEC call this safe because the bytes are 'inside the caller's segment'. That holds in real mode, where offsets wrap. kern_mega defines KERN_BIG and therefore GFX_PLANE, and there a claim's selector limit is the claim's own end. A canvas's last row, or a first row at offset < 3 with odd-phase x, therefore reads outside the limit: #GP inside the decoder. Plausible, not run.
evidence: vga12.inc:2612-2632 four source bytes per group
vga12.inc:2475-2477 groups past the block's end
mega.inc:5968-5970 last selector's limit is the claim's end
SPEC.md:99294-99296 OSAPI_SEG limit runs to the block's end
findings.recommendation: Under %ifdef KERN_MEGA, do one `lsl` of ES where the planar path is armed (vga12.inc:2046-2068), and leave [gfx_blit_pok]=0 when SI-3 underflows or the last row's end+3 passes the limit. Either way, state the 3-byte slack in OSAPI_GFX_BLIT4's contract.
findings.verify_note: kern_mega defines KERN_BIG (kernel.asm:221/240), so GFX_PLANE. vga_blit_prow biases SI back by p>>1 (2574-2576) and reads whole 4-byte groups. mega.inc:5966-5970 says a selector's limit is the claim's own end. No lsl or limit guard exists in vga12.inc (the only KERN_MEGA arm is the DS load at 2585). Still PLAUSIBLE, not run. The real-mode argument in SPEC 5.4.1.3 ('inside the caller's segment') does not carry. The slack at the end is only what the claim's paragraph rounding leaves.

findings.title: gfx_blit1 far-calls the clip-region question twice per band
findings.detail: On kern_big, CLIPQF is `call KERNEL_SEG:cw_gfx_clip_query`, a far call to a shim that near-calls gfx_clip_query: about 170 clocks round trip. gfx_blit1_x asks it at 6019 and again at 6067, and nothing in between can change the answer except the hole arming the first call itself performs. The fix carries the first answer in ZF across the nine pushes, which write no flags. The unarmed path already reaches .clipok with ZF=1. `ja .clipok` already arrives with ZF=0; the fall-throughs that do not (after `jne .okq` on kern_big, after `jc .percol` on kern_small) need `or sp,sp` (ZF=0, 2 bytes). Then the second CLIPQF (5 bytes) can be deleted and `je .rowsall` reads the carried flag.
evidence: vga12.inc:6019-6055 first ask and the paths into .clipok
findings.recommendation: Carry ZF to .clipok and drop the second CLIPQF. Optionally inline the first in .cold (DS = KERNEL_SEG there): +~9 bytes for another ~-110 clocks.
findings.bytes_est: -3 .cold on kern_big (~-170 clocks, ~36 us a band, PREDICTED); -3 on kern_small (~-20 clocks: CLIPQF is an inline cmp there)
findings.verify_note: Confirmed on kern_big: CLIPQF is `call KERNEL_SEG:cw_gfx_clip_query` (vga12.inc:457-459, kernel.asm:7890). Nothing between 6019 and 6067 can change the answer. Of the paths into .clipok, `je .clipok` (ZF=1) and `ja .clipok` (ZF=0) already carry the right flag. Only the `jne .okq` fall-through (ZF=1 though armed) needs `or sp,sp`. Kern_big net is -5+2 = -3. Corrected for kern_small: there CLIPQF is the inline `cmp word [wm_clip_n],0` (5 bytes, vga12.inc:475-477), not a far call. The saving is -5+2 = -3 bytes (not -4) and ~20 clocks a band, not ~170.

findings.title: gfx_points has no planar path: every VGA point is a whole gfx_fill
findings.detail: The gate sends [vid_mono]=0 to .slow, which issues one gfx_pixel per point and pays the full rect machinery. SPEC 5.13 measures 640.87 us per GFX_PIXEL against 165.96 per point on the 1bpp loop. The callers that draw many points (Cyclone, Missile, Tank, os88gfx's GFXE_POINTS sink, the C SDK's os88_gfx_points) get none of the 3.9x on a VGA XT. A planar GFXPT_LOOP body needs nothing the loop lacks: arm Set/Reset = [gfx_color] once (GC0/GC1, as vga_blit_span does); per point do `mov ah,[cs:si+gfx_bitset] / mov al,8 / out dx,ax / xchg [es:di],al`; call vga_gc_reset at .done. ES = VGA_SEG, with the same row table and clip box.
findings.recommendation: Add a fourth loop body in the .vga rung behind the existing depth test. Points that straddle displays keep .slow. Take one gfxbench row on os8088_xt_vga before spending the bytes.
findings.bytes_est: +60..70 .vga (resident on VGA/EGA machines only); ~5-10x per point on VGA, PREDICTED
findings.verify_note: The gate is real: vga12.inc:1350-1365 sends vid_mono=0 to .slow, a gfx_pixel per point (1401-1414). SPEC 5.6.9.2 says only that 'a planar one is gfx_pixel's work either way', with no measurement or refusal of a planar arm, so this is not re-proposing a refused item. gfx_bitset exists (1577). The gain and the +60..70 bytes are PREDICTED. A gfxbench row on os8088_xt_vga should decide it, as the reviewer says.

findings.title: [gfx_color] after gfx_blit4 depends on which path drew
findings.detail: The run paths overwrite [gfx_color] with the last run's colour; the two decoders never touch it. The header and SPEC 5.4 promise 'left holding the last colour drawn', and the SDK contract is silent. A package that does SET_COLOR, BLIT4, FILL therefore gets a fill colour that depends on the adapter, x alignment, run density and whether a region was armed.
findings.recommendation: Preserve it: bank AL in the prologue and restore before kret_bp. Failing that, declare it UNSPECIFIED in SPEC 5.4 and the SDK.
findings.prior_art: Neither GDI BitBlt nor QuickDraw CopyBits changes the pen.
findings.verify_note: vga_blit_span (2343-2344), gfx_blit_run (3245-3250) and gfx_b4piece (6938) store [gfx_color]. sw_blit_row and vga_blit_prow never do. The header (1742-1743) and SPEC 5.4 (4253-4254) both promise 'the last colour drawn'. The two doc fixes below state the current behaviour as UNSPECIFIED. If the preserve fix lands instead, both texts change again.

findings.title: Built-and-off knob bodies double the hot code without shipping its wins
findings.detail: KHP_VGASAVE/VGAFILL/VGAEDGE/VGABLITP/FRAME are kern_mega-only, and KHP_MONORECT/MONOPAT/MONOSCROLL are defined by no kernel. That leaves two bodies at ~15 sites in these files, plus ~240 lines of the 1bpp bank walk that no shipped kern_big runs. Meanwhile its measured -51% on GFX_FILL 64x64 (CGA/Herc, +344 bytes) is the biggest win for the calibration machine. New arguments: (a) VGA rows 3, 6, 8 and 9 (+214) are .vga bytes, which a 1bpp machine slides away, so only VGA/EGA machines pay for them; (b) the shelf already produces false docs (softgfx.inc:445 banner, SPEC 5.7 items 9-10); (c) t_khpknobs proves the arms assemble, not that they draw.
findings.recommendation: Set a dated decision per row: take it into kern_big or delete the arm. No indefinite shelf.
findings.bytes_est: 0 to decide; per row as LAST-DROP-PERF 7.1 prices it
findings.verify_note: kernel.asm:243-297: the vga KHP knobs, KHP_FRAME and KHP_FPG are defined only under KERN_MEGA. MONORECT, MONOSCROLL and MONOPAT are defined by no kernel. The stale softgfx.inc:445 banner is confirmed (fixed below). Already ranked in LAST-DROP-PERF.md 7.1, so this is a call for a dated decision, not a new item.

findings.title: The planar bodies hard-code an 80-byte stride
findings.detail: Every VGA row step in the fill, gray, pattern, save and restore bodies is the ROW_BYTES constant. gfx_blitp's plane-major path reads [vid_stride] and gfx_blit1 reads [vid_rowadd]. The invariant 'every 4-plane surface is 80 bytes a row' is held only by prose (lines 8-9), and that prose is stale. A future 800x600x16 planar mode would shear every fill.
findings.recommendation: Add a check in vid_apply (.ovl): 4 planes implies stride == ROW_BYTES, else refuse the mode. State it in SPEC §5's opening.
findings.verify_note: ROW_BYTES is the step at every listed planar site (vga12.inc:3398-4782). gfx_blitp reads [vid_stride] and gfx_blit1 reads [vid_rowadd]. The prose at lines 8-9 is stale (fixed below). Whether vid_apply sits in .ovl, and so the '+~8 .ovl' figure, was not checked.

findings.title: A right-edge clip forfeits both blit decoders
findings.detail: x+w > [vid_cw] sends the whole block to the per-run path at ~0.5 ms a run. Clamping [gfx_blit_w] to vid_cw - x once (when x >= 0) keeps both decoders and the scanner, because the source stride is BP and is unaffected. Callers clip today, so this mostly lets them stop. An even left clip is a source advance of -x/2 bytes; an odd one can use gfx_b4piece's column logic, which already exists.
evidence: softgfx.inc:962-966 'every caller clips its own blit'
findings.recommendation: Clamp w to the right edge once, before the fast-path tests.

findings.title: The shipped 1bpp XOR interior is a byte loop
findings.detail: The column-major body complements interior bytes one at a time. Every Disk-window selection band and the menu highlight on CGA/Hercules pass through it. The word loop already written for the knob arm (sw_k_xrow) is ~40% cheaper per byte.
findings.recommendation: Port the word body into the shipped column-major .xrow.
findings.verify_note: softgfx.inc:722-727 is `not byte [es:di] / inc di / loop` in the shipped column-major .xrow. The word loop is in the KHP_MONORECT arm. The saving is PREDICTED.

findings.title: gfx_lock's cli...sti is outside CLAUDE.md's short form of the IF rule
findings.detail: gfx_lock uses cli...sti. That is correct: it is task-level only and documents 'IF = 1 on return'. SPEC.md §1 rule 3 already scopes the pushf/cli/popf rule to routines callable from an ISR. CLAUDE.md's restatement drops that scope and reads unconditional.
findings.recommendation: Restore the scope in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md's hard rule ('...in anything an ISR can reach').
findings.verify_note: gfx_lock does use cli...sti (vga12.inc:5084-5127) and documents IF=1 on return. But SPEC.md §1 rule 3 (lines 120-122) scopes the rule to 'any routine callable from an ISR', and gfx_lock is task-level only, so SPEC is not contradicted. Only CLAUDE.md's shortened restatement ('Critical sections are pushf/cli ... popf, never cli/sti') reads unconditional. The fix is one clause in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md ('in anything an ISR can reach'), not a SPEC §1 exception list.

findings.title: vga12.inc is not the module §4 describes
findings.detail: It carries the theme (thm_tab, the live block, thm_set and api_thm_set_x in .cold), all the pens, the lock, the display hooks, gfx_blit1, gfx_points and gfx_spans. SPEC 4096 names the lock, save/restore, scroll and 'vga_rect_setup', which is actually gfx_rect_setup and lives in softgfx.inc.
findings.recommendation: Move the theme to kernel/theme.inc (mind t_hotpar parity) and correct §4.
findings.verify_note: thm_* (vga12.inc:131-195), gfx_pen_* (4827), gfx_points (1324), gfx_spans (3557) and gfx_blit1_x (5901) are all in vga12.inc. vga_rect_setup does not exist, and gfx_rect_setup is softgfx.inc:96. The §4 row is fixed below. Moving the theme to its own file is a separate refactor and not checked against t_hotpar.

findings.title: Comments as archaeology bury the current contract
findings.detail: About 7,200 lines carry roughly 2,000 lines of instructions, and much of the prose is 'it was X until size pass N'. This review found 25+ statements about code that is gone: sw_rect_pl, vid_rpara/vid_rend, gfx_line, gfx_pt_resolve, gfx_ls_addr, the back buffer, bb_*, vga_rect_setup, .lowbss plane rows, and gfx_blit1 'kern_big only'.
findings.recommendation: Move history to SPEC and docs/plans/completed. Keep code comments to the current contract and its invariants. Add a cheap gate: identifiers in comments that are neither symbols in the build's map nor on an allow-list.
findings.verify_note: Borne out: of the reviewer's 30 doc mismatches, the 28 checked all hold. The other two (SPEC 4160 and 6014) needed rewording, not refutation. Five more stale statements turned up in the same blocks (softgfx.inc:207-208 SWM_SOLID, the 941/951 register notes, SPEC 4580 '.lowbss', SPEC 4229/4235 bb_*). The proposed identifier-in-comment gate is not priced.

findings.title: 'Asked the depth before entering the display' is a recurring bug class
findings.detail: The tree's own comments record it at gfx_xor_rect (a reboot), the menu save-under (39.14.8), gfx_blit1's pen (5.4.2.4), gfx_blitp's depth test (5.4.3.4, 'LATENT') and gfx_points (39.14.6). Each whole-shape primitive orders cur_unlazy, display enter and depth dispatch by hand, and each got it wrong once.
findings.recommendation: Give the whole-shape class (xor_rect, save/restore, scroll, blitp, blit4's hook, points) one entry routine or macro that hides, enters and only then dispatches. Add a GFXAUDIT assertion that the depth byte is read only when nested or on one display.
findings.prior_art: Windows GDI cannot reach a DDI entry before it has resolved the DC's PDEVICE: the dispatch target is the device itself.
findings.verify_note: The cited comments (vga12.inc:1376-1387, 4089-4105, and the 5.4.3.4 'LATENT' note at gfx_blitp) record the same ordering bug class. A single entry macro is a design proposal, not checked for bytes.

findings.title: A per-display renderer table instead of per-primitive compares and COLD_SLIDE doors
findings.detail: Each primitive does `cmp [vid_planes],4 / jb / je`, a COLD_SLIDE `jmp X_v` door, and on kern_small a NOVGA_ARM. A table of ~8 near pointers in VID_CTX, filled by vid_apply and swapped by vid_ctx_act, would make each entry `jmp [vid_fn_x]` (cycle-neutral). It would fold in VID_EXT's packed dispatch and make the .vga slide structurally safe, since a 1bpp display's table cannot name .vga.
findings.recommendation: Record for the next time the video layer is opened. The current form is measured and works.
findings.prior_art: Win 3.x DDI function table; GEOS video-driver strategy routine.

findings.title: gfx_clip_run tests every fragment, with no early exit
findings.detail: gfx_clip_run intersects the primitive with all [wm_clip_n] rects: up to 16 at ~150 clocks each, ~0.5 ms per primitive under a full region. If the producer kept the list y-sorted, the walk could stop at the first fragment whose y1 exceeds the primitive's y2. gfx_ls_box and gfx_blit1's .frags would gain the same exit.
findings.recommendation: Sort in wm.inc's region builder and add an early exit here (cross-area: wm).
findings.prior_art: Windows and X11 regions are y-x banded rectangle lists for exactly this.
findings.verify_note: gfx_clip_run (vga12.inc:954-1003) walks all [wm_clip_n] fragments with no early exit. The y-sort is wm.inc's, cross-area, and was not checked.

findings.title: V1 cannot be done by changing gfx_fill itself: kernel callers rely on it preserving registers
findings.detail: New evidence for ABI-BREAK-LIST V1: the kernel's internal callers depend on the preserve-everything contract belonging to the BODY. gfx_hline returns BX from the CX that gfx_fill kept; gfx_xor_strips carries the fill pointer in BP across four calls; gfx_blit_run and gfx_pixel do the same. So V1 has to be a new package-facing entry beside the raw body, not a change to gfx_fill, and should be priced with that cell.
findings.recommendation: Price V1 as a separate cell entry that skips the banking, leaving the internal contract alone.
findings.bytes_est: as V1 (-8 kernel) plus a ~6-byte entry
findings.verify_note: gfx_hline (vga12.inc:1070-1079) returns BX from the CX that gfx_fill preserved (`mov bx,cx` after the call). That is a real internal dependency on the preserve-everything body, so V1 has to be a separate package-facing entry. This is a refinement of ABI-BREAK-LIST V1.

findings.title: Parity pads serve the 16-bit buses, not the 8088 target
findings.detail: These two files hold 12 PARITY pads (~61 sites kernel-wide). They keep hot entries at a pinned address parity for 16-bit-bus fetch. The 8088 fetches one byte at a time and is indifferent, so each pad is a resident byte spent for 8086/V30/286 machines.
findings.recommendation: State the trade in t_hotpar's header and CLAUDE.md so it is visible. Not a recommendation to remove the pads.
